name: The Chair of Saint Peter
dates: Rome, kept since the fourth century
history: A feast not of a piece of furniture but of the mission Christ gave to Peter: ‘You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church.’ The chair, or cathedra, is the sign of a bishop’s authority to teach. The Church honours the ministry of Peter and his successors, the bishops of Rome, as the visible foundation of its unity in faith and charity.
life: The feast is among the oldest in the Roman calendar. A list of Roman feasts from the year 354 already marks 22 February as the day of Peter’s chair. It may have begun as a Christian answer to the pagan custom of feasting for dead relatives at this time of year. For centuries Rome kept two feasts, one on 18 January for Peter’s chair at Rome and one today for his chair at Antioch, where he was held to have first presided; in 1960 they were joined. In Saint Peter’s Basilica, Bernini’s great bronze throne, borne up by four Doctors of the Church, encloses an ancient wooden chair long venerated as Peter’s. Above it a window of golden alabaster shows the Holy Spirit as a dove. It is a day to pray for the Pope and for the Church of Rome, which, in the words of Saint Ignatius of Antioch, presides in love.
prayerTo: Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, the Lord made you the rock of His Church and prayed that your faith would not fail. Pray for our Holy Father the Pope, that he may strengthen his brothers in the faith. Pray for the unity of the Church, and for me, that after every failure I may turn back, as you did, and strengthen others. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the Pope and his intentions, an Our Father, a Hail Mary and a Glory Be, and offer a small sacrifice for the unity of the Church.
meditation: Christ built His Church on a man who had denied Him three times. What does that tell you about what He can build on you?
prayer: O God, who together with the keys of the kingdom of heaven didst bestow on thy blessed Apostle Peter the pontifical power of binding and loosing, grant that by the aid of this intercession, we may be released from the bonds of our sins. Who livest…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
